about.heading: Hybrid glass frameworks
paragraphs: Wenlong Xue works on the chemistry and processing of hybrid glass frameworks, MOF glasses, and amorphous proton conductors. The research connects coordination-network design with glass formation, mechanochemistry, melt processing, thin-film preparation, and structure-property analysis.

A central theme is the transformation of ordered crystalline frameworks into disordered but functional materials. These hybrid glasses combine local coordination order with processability, mechanical stability, and transport properties that are difficult to access in conventional crystalline solids.

Current work at KU Leuven focuses on directly synthesised amorphous networks, local structure and transport mechanisms, and routes for integrating proton-conducting hybrid glasses into energy and separation technologies.

research.heading: Research
research.intro: Research is organised around the synthesis, structure, and processing of coordination networks across crystalline and amorphous states.

items.title: Amorphous coordination networks
items.text: Direct synthesis and transformation routes are used to access bulk hybrid glasses and disordered coordination networks without relying only on traditional melt-quenching.

items.title: Local structure and transport
items.text: Synchrotron PDF, XAS, solid-state NMR, impedance spectroscopy, and modelling are combined to understand how local order supports proton and ion transport.
items.imageAlt: Abstract scattering rings and transport pathways

items.title: Processing for energy devices
items.text: Thin films, membranes, and patterned architectures are developed to connect hybrid glass chemistry with medium-temperature fuel cells, electrolysers, and separation systems.
items.imageAlt: Abstract hybrid glass film device architecture

contact.heading: Collaborations and enquiries
contact.text: Research discussions, synchrotron proposals, student enquiries, and collaborative projects in hybrid glasses, MOF processing, and proton-conducting materials are welcome.
